claims.text: Q235 corrosion resistance across room- and high-temperature regimes is governed by the formation and stability of an iron-oxide scale.
Iron-oxide scale nucleates preferentially at impurity sites such as MnS inclusions.
At room temperature, slow oxidation at impurity sites produces a compact, adherent, protective film.
At 700–900 °C, accelerated and spatially uneven oxidation promotes oxide-film spallation.
Oxide-film spallation exposes the Q235 substrate locally and accelerates its corrosion-related degradation.
Pre-exposure Q235 contains typical microstructural impurities, including MnS inclusions.
The Q235 starting material has no pre-formed oxide scale.
MnS inclusions serve as nucleation centers for oxide-film development.
Slow room-temperature oxidation produces a thin, uniform iron-oxide film that passivates the surface.
Rapid elevated-temperature oxidation produces a thicker, porous, and non-uniform oxide film.
Stress arising from oxide volumetric expansion and film inhomogeneity causes spallation.
At room temperature, Q235 will develop a stable protective oxide film.
During 700–900 °C salt exposure, Q235 will develop a thicker but porous and spallation-prone film with localized degradation.
Changing MnS content or controlling inclusion effects will alter film uniformity, adherence, or localized corrosion relative to typical-impurity Q235.
The proposed mechanism applies to Q235 with standard impurity levels in oxygen-rich air.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to steels with substantially altered impurity profiles or under non-oxidative atmospheres.
Other impurities and grain-boundary characteristics may also contribute to oxide formation and stability.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies controlled annealing before exposure, the baseline is defined as not having undergone controlled annealing, and the falsification design says that all specimens are annealed. These definitions do not identify one consistent reference condition.
The predicted outcome uses a sample with modified impurity content or inclusion-controlling pretreatment as the reference, whereas the baseline is typical-impurity Q235 without controlled annealing.
